title: Audit and migrate legacy TLS bindings and token encoders to modern libraries
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Perform a cross-service audit and migration to modern TLS/crypto bindings and token libraries (OpenSSL -> BoringTLS/BoringSSL-compatible shim where appropriate, jwt/oauth libraries replacement, SAML adapters remediation). Goal is to remove fragile transitive dependencies, fix parsing edge-cases observed in customer SSO flows, and eliminate CVE exposure windows while preserving backwards compatibility for existing service-to-service authentication.
acceptance_criteria: All services that perform token verification use approved library set or a vetted compatibility shim
No failing production SSO flows in canary region after rollout
Automated regression suite (unit + integration) added and green in CI
Runtime memory and latency overhead <= 5% compared to baseline for critical paths
Security review completed and signoff from SecOps
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Audit runtime binary deps and dependency tree across gateway, auth-proxy, console, and runtime agents
Phase 2: Introduce compatibility adapter layer for services that require incremental rollout
Phase 3: Replace library calls and update wrappers; run CI/regression and perf harness
Use feature-flagged rollout with route-level canaries (console -> dedicated -> hosted)
progress_updates: 2026-02-17: Created ticket after post-mortem on SSO parsing mismatch; initial audit started
2026-02-22: Completed inventory: 24 services use jwt-go (v3.x), 8 services rely on openssl via native bindings, 5 use legacy saml libraries with custom patches
2026-02-28: Prototype shim implemented in auth-common: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-common/pull/402 (perf baseline + compatibility tests)
2026-03-05: Benchmarks show BoringTLS-compatible shim reduces syscall overhead on handshake by ~12% in microbench for small payloads
2026-03-10: Began staged rollout to dev and canary; first service (gateway-auth) flipped behind feature flag; initial canary logs show no auth-errors
review_feedback: Security review (K. Liu) 2026-02-29: requested expanded token canonicalization tests for unicode-mapped input
PM review (M. Chen) 2026-03-03: requested rollout gating tied to console-usage telemetry
Design/UX (R. Patel) 2026-03-04: confirmed no end-user changes; error surfaces should preserve existing messages for backwards-compatible SSO errors
testing_plan: Unit tests for token parsing edge-cases (NULs, unicode, padded base64)
Integration tests exercising SAML assertion exchanges end-to-end against staging IdP
Canary traffic at 5% for 48 hours with synthetic user journeys (console, API key rotation, dedicated connection flows)
Performance regression harness measured across 24-hour steady-state and peak burst scenarios
rollback_plan: Feature-flag immediate rollback via config endpoint
If increased 5xx auth-errors or latency >5% observed in canary, flip flag and investigate via traceIDs
notes: Trade-off: full switch to new library in one go risks wide blast radius; using compatibility shim increases code surface but enables incremental verification
Decision: prefer vetted shim + short-lived adapter wrappers over ad-hoc native openssl upgrades to avoid duplicated effort across runtimes
Follow-up: schedule post-rollout review to codify approved library versions and add to dependency-policy docs
